questions.problem:
What is the explicit formula for the $n$th term of the sequence

$$
f(n+1)=f(n)-\frac{3}{4},\,\,f(1)=-\frac{5}{4},\,\,n\ge 1?
$$
questions.worked_solution:
The explicit formula for the $n$th term of an arithmetic sequence (in function notation) is

$$
f(n)=f(1)+(n-1)d,\,n\ge 1,
$$

so we need to determine the first term $f(1)$ and the common difference $d.$

We are given that the first term is $f(1)=-\frac{5}{4},$ and we can use the recursive rule to compute the second term, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(2) & =f(1)-\frac{3}{4} \\  & =-\frac{5}{4}-\frac{3}{4} \\  & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

Using the first and second terms, we can compute the common difference:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =f(2)-f(1) \\  & =-2-(-\frac{5}{4}) \\  & =-\frac{3}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we substitute $f(1)=-\frac{5}{4}$ and $d=-\frac{3}{4}$ into the formula for the $n$th term:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(n) & =f(1)+(n-1)d \\  & =-\frac{5}{4}+(n-1)(-\frac{3}{4}) \\  & =-\frac{5}{4}-\frac{3}{4}n+\frac{3}{4} \\  & =-\frac{3}{4}n-\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the formula for the $n$th term is

$$
f(n)=-\frac{3}{4}n-\frac{1}{2},\,n\ge 1.
$$

questions.problem: The formula for the $n$th term of an arithmetic sequence is $f(n)=2n-1$ for $n\ge 1.$  What is the recursive formula for this sequence?
questions.worked_solution:
The recursive formula for an arithmetic sequence is as follows:

$$
f(n+1)=f(n)+d,\,f(1)=___\,,\,n\ge 1
$$

To complete the formula, we need to work out the first term and common difference. The first two terms are

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1) & =2(1)-1=1 \\ f(2) & =2(2)-1=3\end{aligned}
$$

and the common difference is

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =f(2)-f(1) \\  & =3-1 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the first term is $f(1)=1$ and the common difference is $d=2.$ Therefore, the recursive formula is as follows:

$$
f(n+1)=f(n)+2,\,f(1)=1,\,n\ge 1
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the following arithmetic sequence:

$$
{a}_{n+1}={a}_{n}-6,\,\,{a}_{1}=5,\,\,n\ge 1
$$

The explicit formula for the $n$th term is

${a}_{n}=$
{{field-1}}$,\,n\ge 1.$
questions.worked_solution:
The explicit formula for the $n$th term of an arithmetic sequence is

$$
{a}_{n}={a}_{1}+(n-1)d,\,n\ge 1,
$$

so we need to determine the first term ${a}_{1}$ and the common difference $d.$

We are given that the first term is ${a}_{1}=5,$ and we can use the recursive rule to compute the second term, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{2} & ={a}_{1}-6 \\  & =5-6 \\  & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

Using the first and second terms, we can compute the common difference:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & ={a}_{2}-{a}_{1} \\  & =-1-5 \\  & =-6\end{aligned}
$$

Now we substitute ${a}_{1}=5$ and $d=-6$ into the formula for the $n$th term:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}+(n-1)d \\  & =5+(n-1)(-6) \\  & =5-6n+6 \\  & =11-6n\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the formula for the $n$th term is

$$
{a}_{n}=11-6n,\,n\ge 1.
$$
